html:
The Kuku Yalanji are an Aboriginal Australian people of the rainforest of far north Queensland, from around Mossman north through the Daintree and Bloomfield rivers toward Cooktown.

They lived in and from the rainforest and the reef coast, and their country includes Mossman Gorge. Their neighbours were the Guugu Yimithirr around Cooktown, the Djabugay and Yidinji to the south, and the Mbabaram inland.

The Palmer River gold rush of 1873 brought thousands of miners through their country, and Cooktown was founded as its port. Tin miners and timber getters followed. A Lutheran mission opened on the Bloomfield River in the 1880s, today the community of Wujal Wujal. Since 1988 much of their land lies in the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area.
sum: The Kuku Yalanji are an Aboriginal Australian people of the rainforest of far north Queensland, from around Mossman north through the Daintree and Bloomfield rivers toward Cooktown.
